outcome: Cesarean delivery complications (cystotomies, bowel deserosalization, vaginal lacerations)
cohort: The study included 11 women (18 pregnancies, 15 live newborns) with neuropathic bladder due to spinal dysraphism who underwent pediatric lower urinary tract reconstruction, subsequently became pregnant, and delivered via cesarean section at the study institution between July 2001 and June 2016.
finding: Women with neuropathic bladder and lower urinary tract reconstruction have high rates of complications during pregnancy and cesarean delivery, with worse complications observed in those with prolonged labor, previous CD, or a history of noncompliance.
mod_finding: All births in the study were via cesarean delivery, and complications such as cystotomies and urinary fistulae occurred exclusively during emergent cesarean deliveries.
gest_age: Gestational age was collected, with 53.3% of births being term.
